topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the session by framing how the lecture will integrate previously learned components to explore the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate immune recognition of infection and damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how pattern recognition receptors and downstream intracellular pathways detect microbial molecular patterns and cellular damage to trigger immune activation.

topics.label: Cellular activation, leukocyte trafficking, and systemic inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how activated sentinel cells direct the recruitment of circulating leukocytes into tissues, facilitate antigen drainage, and can trigger severe systemic pathology.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory states
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the passive and active mechanisms that terminate inflammation, drive tissue healing, and lead to persistent or protective chronic inflammatory responses.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture and previews the next topic on the complement system.
